root_cause: Shell consumes the 'settings' query in an effect (Shell.tsx:2585-2594: openSettings, then delete the param with a replace). Another effect closes Settings on any pathname change while useNavigationType() is POP (Shell.tsx:896-899). The pass-22 fix carried the query through the redirects but did not cover this ordering.

title: Legal re-scan can silently replace extracted contract values (Office lease $90,000 became $9,000)
root_cause: LegalRepos.upsertContract keeps stored fields only when the new extraction is empty; 'A different value still replaces it, since a document can be amended' (packages/db/src/legal.ts:191-210). It does not compare the item's revision with the stored analyzedRevision, so a re-scan of an unchanged file with a different (model-noisy) extraction overwrites money values and dates with no notice.
verification: OBSERVED by J2 once (before/after screenshots: $90,000 to $9,000, $30,000 to $3,000, titles lost the MOCK prefix, a start date moved). Overwrite rule CONFIRMED in code (db/legal.ts:191-210, legal-tools.ts:353-395). The demo model is scripted and non-deterministic, so real-model behaviour is UNVERIFIED. Rated P2 for that reason; raise to P1 if a real-model run reproduces it.
files_to_change: packages/db/src/legal.ts (when input.revision equals stored.analyzedRevision and a stored value differs, keep the stored value and return the proposed one as a change; replace only when the revision is newer)
packages/adapters/src/legal-tools.ts:353-395 (surface 'proposed change' in the tool result so the agent tells the user)
packages/db/src/legal.test.ts (same revision with a different value keeps the stored value; newer revision replaces it)
reach: Everyone who re-scans Legal; the numbers are money on a contract list.
acceptance_criteria: Same-revision upsert with a different valueCents keeps the stored value (unit test).
A newer revision with a different value replaces it and the agent's result lists the change.
